title: Move traversal and keyed acyclicity primitives into the graph layer
description:
Give the graph layer the primitives command handlers currently hand-roll: depth-bounded traversal and a string-keyed acyclicity check. Refactor the three ad-hoc implementations onto them.

## Background

`commands/graph.rs:42-145` (`build_dependency_tree`, `show_dependencies_with_depth`) hand-rolls forward traversal with `load_issue` calls interleaved per node, while the reverse direction (`show_rdeps_with_depth`, `graph.rs:147-191`) correctly delegates to `DependencyGraph`. Root cause: `graph/mod.rs` offers no depth-bounded primitive. Separately, `batch_create.rs:590` (`detect_cycle`) and `breakdown.rs:546` (`first_child_cycle`) each hand-roll DFS over symbolic graphs (keys/indices) because the graph layer only accepts nodes with real ids.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: The graph layer provides a depth-bounded traversal primitive used by both the forward and reverse dependency views; no command handler contains its own recursive or iterative graph walk.
- [hard] REQ-2: Dependency-tree building loads all issues once up front and traverses in memory; no storage reads occur inside traversal.
- [hard] REQ-3: A generic keyed acyclicity check in the graph layer replaces the symbolic-graph DFS in batch creation and in breakdown child splicing, with cycle-path error reporting at least as specific as today's.
- [hard] REQ-4: Unlimited-depth forward traversal returns the same node set as the existing transitive-dependencies primitive, verified by a test.

## Notes

Keep `graph/` pure and generic: the keyed check should work over any `(K, Vec<K>)` adjacency, so both callers and future symbolic graphs (template roles) can reuse it. CLI output formats must not change.
